estimates.note: Emax doesn't publish how the 45.5 mm splits between the body and the shaft. 31 mm for the base and bell, leaving 14.5 mm of shaft, is a typical split for a 2814, to be checked against Emax's side photos

Gemfan publishes only the size, bore and weight. The 9 mm hub and 22 mm blade width come from a retailer's spec block (rotorvillage.ca), which looks copied from Gemfan. The hub diameter isn't published anywhere; 15 mm is a guess for a 10-inch tri-blade
Holybro gives 6 mm overall; the split between the board and its parts, and the hole pattern sitting centered along the 48 mm length, come from Holybro's stack STEP, measured roughly

Not published, so traced from iFlight's top-down product render (https://cdn.iflight.com/store/product/Drone-Frame/XL10-V6/XL10-V6-B3.png) with the 420 mm diagonal between motors as the scale. The motors came out 295.5 x 298.9 mm apart against iFlight's 297 x 297, so the scale is good to about 1%. Arms 15 mm wide (15.1 to 16.4 along their length); body plates 36 mm wide, narrowing to 29 mm from about 70 mm ahead of the center, reaching 154 mm ahead of the motors' center and 62 mm behind, not counting the camera cage and the XT60 mount. The motor pads weren't measured; 34 mm is a guess that just carries a 35 mm motor
The 8 mm height is split as a 1.6 mm board, 5 mm of parts on top and 1.4 mm below. ARK doesn't give the hole size either; its own RIG5 build uses M3 screws, so the holes are taken as 3.2 mm
The microSD socket's height underneath isn't given; 1.5 mm is a guess
The board and the chip, without header pins
The 11.3 mm overall depth minus the lens stack and the board
The drawing doesn't give the board thickness or the USB and Ethernet stack's height; these are typical for a Raspberry Pi

The HAT looks HAT-sized in Heltec's photos, so it's drawn as the standard Raspberry Pi HAT (65 x 56.5 mm, holes on 58 x 49 mm), with the card lying on it and a 40-pin header underneath. Heltec only lists Pi 1 to 4 for the HAT
Physics, not a datasheet: half the wavelength at 915 MHz. A real antenna will be close to this, and it needs a spot clear of the props and the carbon
The taller of the two published heights
A box roughly the size of a small claw with its servos
